newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Asian airlines protest Australia/HK charges.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Asian airlines protest Australia/HK charges.

text.p: Major airlines in the Asia/Pacific region said on Friday they had formally protested about higher user charges at Australian airports as well as possible increases at Hong Kong's new airport.

Orient Airlines Association (OAA) chairman James Strong, who is also managing director of Australian flagship Qantas Airways Ltd, said the OAA had written to Australian transport minister John Sharp objecting to a 10.8 percent increase in charges ahead of the privatisation of Australian airports.

"We have written to him reflecting the concerns of the airlines represented in OAA," Strong told a news conference following a meeting of OAA executive members at the Gold Coast, south-east of Brisbane.
Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd chief executive Rod Eddington said OAA had also formally written to the Hong Kong Secretary of Economic Services objecting to proposed increases at Chep Lap Kok.
He said there was speculcation that airlines using the new airport could pay twice the fee applicable at Kai Tak.
"This is clearly a major blow to operators. We have formally written objecting to the proposed charges."
Eddington said the airlines were taking a pro-active stance ahead of possible increases which could take effect in late 1998.
"We are concerned now because we are a thin-margin business," he said. Eddington becomes executive chairman of Ansett Airways Ltd in January 1997.
The OAA met on Friday to consider several resolutions including a change of name to the Association of Asia/Pacific Airlines.
Ansett, a joint venture between News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd, was admitted as a member at the two-day meeting.
Strong said fuel costs were not discussed at the meeting but the issue was a major concern to OAA members.
